subject: Territory evidence handoff and private-deploy detail request
messages:
From: Claire Zhao <claire@medisource.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medisource.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency evidence request + CAIQ/SIG items (Medisource pilot)

Hi Olga / Jonas —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As part of our pilot approval we need a compact evidence pack addressing residency and VPC/private-connect controls so our security reviewers can complete the CAIQ/SIG mapping. Can you provide the following by EOD next Wednesday (2026-11-18)?

- SOC 2 (latest) or SOC 2 bridge letter and the CAIQ index entries mapped to your control IDs.
- A short statement confirming which physical regions host customer-controlled workloads for a pinned model (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) and the default egress behavior.
- PrivateLink/VPC peering diagram for the hosted Private deployment, including VPC endpoint names and whether traffic traverses our peering (we need assurance that no cross-border egress occurs for EU-designated tenants).
- Keystore/keys: operator access model, HSM/KMS location, and a roster of any human operator accounts that can access key material (for auditors).
- A short runbook snippet showing how failover/rollbacks are executed for a Private deployment (canary, fallback to hosted-compatible model, and the timeline).

I attached our initial SIG worksheet so you can mark the rows you can evidence directly. If any of this needs an NDA or separate upload, let me know.

Claire
Security Program Manager
Medisource

Attachment: Medisource_SIG_Questions_v1.xlsx

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhao <claire@medisource.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency evidence request + CAIQ/SIG items (Medisource pilot)

Claire —

Thanks — we can provide the artifacts you listed. High-level plan and owners below; will push a consolidated packet and links by COB 2026-11-16 (earlier if we get the updated SIG sheet back with row IDs).

Owners / deliverables:
- SOC 2 & CAIQ mapping: Marissa (attestation + control mapping PDF).
- Region hosting statement + egress table: Jonas (architecture diagram + signed statement).
- Privatelink/VPC peering diagram + operator roster: Rishi (diagram + keystore manifest).
- Runbook excerpt (failover/rollback): Olga (ops playbook snippet + retention notes).

One ask: can you confirm whether Medisource will accept a redacted SOC 2 (redacting customer lists) or do you need full PCAOB report? That impacts our legal upload process.

I'll start assembling a Drive folder (shared link below) and attach a stubbed checklist to this thread.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: residency-evidence-checklist.pdf
Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Medisource/Residency-Evidence-Setup

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: artifact breakdown for Medisource ask

Folks —

Quick technical breakdown we should include in the packet so auditors have actionable items (I pulled examples from prior packs):

- Region statement: short table with region code, service role (compute, kv cache, storage), and customer-data residency guarantee for pinned model. Explicit callout: default control plane metadata (non-customer) may traverse US regions; customer payloads for EU tenants never egress EU nodes.
- PrivateLink diagram: VPC CIDR, endpoint IDs (redacted), peering path showing no internet egress, and the TLS termination point. Highlight NAT/Gateway placement and whether egress logging is enabled.
- Keystore: show KMS ARN prefix, HSM vendor, and operator access model (no direct human HSM access; operator-run jobs require two-person approval; recorded in audit logs). Provide a CSV manifest of operator accounts with role and justification (redact email suffixes as needed).
- Runbook: include a canary rollback path with estimated RTO/RPO, who triggers failover, and the automatic fallback policy to a verified smaller quantized model.

I'll prepare the network sketch and the region table. Rishi, can you export the keystore manifest (last rotation snapshot) and the operator roster? Marissa — SOC2 mapping please.

-Jonas
Lead Infra Architect

From: Claire Zhao <claire@medisource.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, security@medisource.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency evidence request + CAIQ/SIG items (Medisource pilot)

Thanks Olga/Jonas — quick clarifying Qs from our infra/security reviewer:

1) For the keystore operator manifest: are the operator accounts Redwood employees or third-party vendor accounts? We need to know if any non-Redwood staff have HSM key access for this environment.
2) For the PrivateLink diagram: will the peering create any cross-border route tables during failover (e.g., if an EU node degrades, could traffic be routed to us-east temporarily)? If yes, we need the exact conditions and SLAs.

If you can include short one-liners next to each artifact (e.g., "operator roster: Redwood employees only; no third-party human access") that will speed our review.

Claire

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhao <claire@medisource.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2026 15:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency evidence request + CAIQ/SIG items (Medisource pilot)

Claire —

Please find the consolidated evidence packet attached and the Drive folder linked above. Quick answers inline to your clarifying Qs, plus a short artifact map below.

Inline answers:
- Keystore operator accounts: Redwood employees only. We do not grant direct HSM access to third-party contractors for customer keystores. Operator manifest (keystore-operator-manifest.csv) includes role, SSO ID (redacted), date of last training, and approval ticket ID. All entries are audited in the HSM access ledger.
- PrivateLink failover behavior: automatic regional failover to an adjacent Redwood region is supported for critical infrastructure, however customer-designated pinned workloads will not be auto-routed across geopolitical boundaries. For Medisource EU-pinned tenants, failover will prefer EU zones; cross-border failover to US only occurs under documented emergency escalation with SLA acknowledgement and explicit written consent. The runbook excerpt and fallback policy (privatelink-runbook-2026-11.pdf) are attached.

Artifact map (attachments + Drive):
- redwood_residency_evidence_packet_20261116.zip — contains: region-hosting-statement.pdf; CAIQ-index-mapping.xlsx; network-diagrams/privatelink_eu_us.pdf; keystore-operator-manifest.csv (redacted); soc2-bridge-letter-redacted.pdf.
- privatelink-runbook-2026-11.pdf — canary/rollback steps, failover triggers, RTO/RPO numbers, and test schedule.

Related links: shared Drive and DocuSign envelope for attestation (we include a short signature page so your security lead can accept the packet).

If you want, Marissa can sign the attestation PDF; otherwise we can route a DocuSign to your security mailbox. Thanks for the clear list — happy to hop on a 30m call if your reviewers prefer walkthroughs.

Best,
Olga
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_residency_evidence_packet_20261116.zip; privatelink-runbook-2026-11.pdf; keystore-operator-manifest.csv
Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/Medisource/Residency-Evidence-20261116
